info.title: Sercha API
info.description: The public Sercha API. Every request runs as the caller and sees only what the caller is granted.

post.description: OAuth 2.0 token endpoint. A service account uses grant_type=client_credentials with its client_id and client_secret; an interactive client exchanges an authorization code (with PKCE code_verifier) or a refresh_token. Send the returned access_token as a Bearer token.

parameters.description: Redirect URI used for the code
parameters.name: redirect_uri

post.description: Authenticate with email and password to receive a JWT token
Exchange a refresh token for a new JWT token

get.description: Get the currently authenticated user's profile

post.description: Runs one SerchaQL statement or script as the caller. A SELECT returns rows; SHOW and DESCRIBE return their listings; DDL needs an admin. describe serchaql (MCP) or the SerchaQL reference lists what the language accepts. With ?explain=true the plan is returned instead of rows.

parameters.description: The statement: serchaql text, or ir
parameters.name: request

get.description: Saved queries with typed parameters (CREATE TOOL), with each one's description, parameters and an example call.

post.description: Runs the tool's query with args bound to its parameters (defaults fill the rest). The response is the query response plus the tool name and the statement that ran.

get.description: The corpora the caller can read, by id and name.

Returns everything an admin needs to see about one corpus in a single screen: its sources, bound ontology (the PINNED version snapshot when the binding has one, otherwise the live draft), every entity's full extraction context, edges, structures, hints, attached datasets, the views that read it, and the full SerchaQL DDL that recreates it.
get.summary: Get the catalogue corpus hub detail for one corpus

get.description: The labels and descriptions readers see for a dataset table and its visible columns, with the layers they come from (tenant overlay, connector pack, table catalogue) and, for a connector table, its origin. Columns a connector pack hides are not listed. A missing, internal or not-enabled connector table is 404 (admin only)

parameters.description: Dataset table name, with or without the data. prefix
parameters.name: table

post.description: Runs one read-only SELECT as the caller and writes the whole result to object storage: through the dataset engine (CSV or Parquet, no row cap) when the query reads `data.<table>` datasets alone, else through the query engine as CSV parts under the server's row cap. Returns the export (202 while running; 200 when it finished within wait_seconds) with presigned download links once it has succeeded.

parameters.description: The SELECT, format and optional cap
parameters.name: request

get.description: The caller's export: its status and, once it has succeeded, presigned GET links for every file and the metadata sidecar (signed on each call, valid for at most an hour). wait_seconds (max 60) waits for a running export. Another user's export is a 404.

parameters.description: Wait up to this long for a running export
parameters.name: wait_seconds

get.description: Get a list of all configured data sources with sync status

post.description: Create a new data source (admin only)

get.description: Get a data source by ID

delete.description: Delete a data source by ID (admin only). This also removes all indexed documents from this source.

409.description: Source in use by one or more corpuses

post.description: Trigger a sync operation for a specific source (admin only)

get.description: Get the current sync state and statistics for a specific source. Returns the last sync time, status, and document/chunk counts from the most recent sync operation.

post.description:
Cancels an in-flight sync for a source. Stops the running sync's
work and marks its state as cancelled. No-op if no sync is running.

Accepts one or more documents for a push-provider source (see POST /sources with provider_type=push) and enqueues each for ingest through the same index/claim/extract path a pulled document takes. Returns 202 Accepted: the document rows exist and their raw bytes are retained, but nothing has been normalised, indexed or extracted yet. Poll GET /api/v1/documents/{id} and read ingest_status ("processing" / "indexed" / "failed") to find out when a document became searchable. Re-pushing the same external_id is idempotent and returns the same document_id. Admin only - see the RequireAdmin wiring at setupRoutes for why a pushing service's m2m token must resolve to a users row with Role=admin. Bytes travel base64-encoded in JSON; see the doc comment body below for why that was chosen over multipart/form-data. Body limited to pushDocumentMaxBodyBytes (larger than the default 10 MiB, since base64 inflates size by roughly a third).
post.summary: Push documents to a push source

400.description: Invalid request, unsupported mode, non-push source, or missing push root container

503.description: Task queue not configured, or document retention disabled

get.description: Get all documents indexed from a specific source with pagination support. Optionally filter to a subset of containers via the container_ids query parameter (comma-separated).

parameters.description: Maximum number of documents to return (default 20, max 100)
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Comma-separated container IDs to filter by (omit for all containers)
parameters.name: container_ids

400.description: Missing source ID or invalid parameters

404.description: No such document, or its bytes are not retained

blob_retention_status.description:
BlobRetentionStatus records the outcome of the sync orchestrator's
blob-store write for this document's raw bytes (SD-109). See
BlobRetentionStatus's own doc comment for the three values. Defaults
to BlobRetentionUnset ("") for every document written before this
field existed and for any document retention did not apply to.

container_id.description:
ContainerID is the internal source_containers.id of the leaf container
this document belongs to. Its lifecycle has two phases:

 1. Connector phase - a connector may initially populate this with a
    provider-side reference (e.g. OneDrive parentReference.id), or leave
    it empty. It also sets Change.ContainerProviderRef on the emitted
    Change so the orchestrator knows the raw provider ref.

 2. Orchestrator phase - before the membership-write step the sync
    orchestrator resolves Change.ContainerProviderRef (or falls back to
    this field if the connector set it directly) to an internal
    source_containers row, lazily upserting intermediate rows as needed,
    and overwrites this field with the resolved internal id.

Adapters that read Document.ContainerID at runtime (postgres store, graph
queries, corpus membership checks, MCP tools) always see the internal id.
Empty string means "no container scope" or "the connector does not
surface containers".

content_hash.description:
ContentHash is the hex sha256 of the document's NORMALISED text - the
same digest the organise op's duplicate pre-pass keys on. Written at
ingest where the normalised text exists (Step 6c-ii of
processAddOrUpdate); "" means not yet computed (pre-migration rows,
or a normalisation that produced no text) and must be treated as
unhashable, never as a hash: two ""s matching is not a duplicate.

group.description:
Group is the group a pushed document was sent with (the partition key
under PARTITION BY GROUP), recorded on the document itself so it
survives whether or not a group-partitioned corpus claims the document
yet. A corpus created later, and REPARTITION, derive their per-corpus
document_groups rows from it. "" means pushed without a group, and is
always "" for a pulled document: connectors never supply one.

ingest_status.description:
IngestStatus says whether this document is searchable yet (SD-109's
async push path). See IngestStatus's own doc comment for the three
values and why the distinction had to exist.

The Go zero value is "" rather than IngestStatusIndexed, which does
NOT mean a fourth state: it means a caller constructed a Document
without an opinion, which every pull-sync path does. Normalised to
IngestStatusIndexed by IngestStatusOrDefault, which the persistence
adapters call on the way in, so the column keeps the same invariant
the migration's DEFAULT establishes and no row is ever written with an
empty status.

path.description:
Path is the connector's chosen display path or URL for the document
(often the web URL). Used for UI display and human-readable
identification.

x-enum-comments.SeatAdmin: the admin role: all four plus settings

x-enum-descriptions: the admin role: all four plus settings

connection_id.description: ConnectionID references the connector connection for authentication

connectors.description:
Connectors are the connector packs whose tables this source lands
rows in: its own first, then the ones it includes (a GitHub source
also lands git history). Empty for a source with no pack.

warning.description:
Warning surfaces a completed-but-suspicious sync (SD-123): the sync
finished cleanly yet enumerated zero documents while the source holds
zero local documents. That combination is almost always a misconfigured
container ref or a stale delta cursor, never a healthy no-op, so it is
carried on the state payload rather than buried in a log line. Cleared
at the start of every sync run.

documents_unchanged.description:
DocumentsUnchanged counts changes whose stored document already had
the same content, title, path, type, container and metadata, so the
orchestrator skipped them before normalising, storing or extracting.

entitlements.description: Entitlements and SeatType (SD-160 v3) let the Team page show seats.

pinned_version.description:
PinnedVersion is the `"v<n>"` label of the pinned version, or "" when
the binding is unpinned (draft).

structures.description:
Structures carries each declared entity.Structure marshalled as-is
(name, levels, cleanup): the UI renders the structure tree directly
from the domain shape rather than a bespoke projection.

version_number.description: VersionNumber is the pinned version's number, or 0 for a draft.

set_by_name.description:
SetByName is the display name or email of SetBy when it resolves to a
known user; empty when it does not (a deleted user, a system write,
or the user lookup is not wired).

ddl.description:
DDL is the full SerchaQL script that recreates this corpus: ontology,
entities with their EXTRACT/SENSITIVE annotations, structures, edges,
the corpus declaration, BIND/REBIND, every hint, attached datasets and
views. Rendered by serchaql.RenderCorpusDDL.

is_under.description:
IsUnder marks an internal part_of edge that an UNDER modifier produced;
the DDL renders it as UNDER on the child entity, not as CREATE EDGE.

ddl.description:
DDL is this entity's CREATE ENTITY statement plus its ALTER ENTITY
statements, rendered standalone.

description.description:
Description is the entity's extraction-prompt description. Reported
"" when the stored value is the internal "__lazy__" marker (see Lazy).

hint_keys.description:
HintKeys lists the invocation keys of the binding's hints that target
this entity `(extract_internals:<LocalID>` and, for an
extract-per-child root, `extract_internals:<LocalID>.<Child>`).

lazy.description:
Lazy is true when the entity's stored Description is the "__lazy__"
convention value.

natural_key.description:
NaturalKey is the ordered natural-key column list; empty when the
entity declares none.

parent.description:
Parent is the UNDER parent's local id, resolved from the internal
part_of edge this entity's child sits on. Empty for a root or a free
entity.

group_field.description:
GroupField is the field a document's group arrives in, under the
"group" or "group_structure" strategies.

structure.description:
Structure is `"<ontology>.<structure>"` when the corpus organises by a
declared STRUCTURE, under the "structure" or "group_structure"
strategies.

generation_template.description:
GenerationTemplate is set for a GENERATE-backed column; empty
otherwise.

source_kind.description:
SourceKind, SourceEntity, SourceProperty and JoinEdge describe a
property copied or joined from elsewhere (extends-via, pack entity
injection); empty when the property is extracted directly.

connector.description:
Connector is the provider type as written in CREATE CORPUS ON, e.g.
"onedrive" or "push": the executor matches a target's connector
against the provider type, so this is what the DDL must carry.

connector_label.description:
ConnectorLabel is the provider's display name for people, e.g.
"OneDrive" or "Pushed documents".

reads.description:
Reads lists every corpus and view name the body reads, at any depth
(the same walk serchaql's dataset_acl.go bodyReadable uses).

key.description: Key is the full object key in the export bucket.

name.description:
Name is the object's name within the export (its key relative to the
export's data prefix).

url.description:
URL is a presigned GET for the object, filled when a status is read,
never stored.

bytes.description: Bytes is the total size of the data files.

bytes_scanned.description: BytesScanned is what the dataset engine read, when it ran the query.

column_policy.description:
ColumnPolicy is the fingerprint of the AI product column policy the
export ran under (SD-193); empty for an unrestricted caller. A
restricted caller reads only exports made under its own policy, so a
product cannot fetch files its owner exported with full access.

columns.description:
Columns is the columns block (what each output column means), as the
query and export tools return it.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is when the URLs handed out by this read stop working.

note.description: Note explains a fallback or a cap in plain words.

query.description:
Query is the SELECT as submitted; ExecutedQuery is what ran, with any
row cap applied.

row_cap.description: RowCap is the cap applied, 0 for none.

row_count.description: RowCount is the number of rows written.

sidecar.description:
Sidecar is the metadata file written beside the data (query, schema,
columns), with its presigned URL filled per read.

source_tables.description:
SourceTables are the dataset tables the query read, directly or
through views, recorded when the export starts. Every status read
and file read checks them against the connector lock again, so files
written while a connector was enabled are not served once it is not.
Absent from a manifest written before they were recorded (and from
one whose query reads no dataset table); the query text is then read
for them instead.

truncated.description: Truncated is true when the cap cut the result.

name.description:
Name is the column identifier as it appears in the result set, e.g.
"clause_id", "severity_level", "is_root". Must be non-empty.

type.description:
Type is the value kind for this column. Consumers read the matching
field on [TypedValue] based on this discriminator.

catalogue.description: Catalogue is the table catalogue's own comment, empty when none.

label.description: Label, Description and Unit are what readers see.

overlay.description: Overlay is the tenant's entry, nil when it has none.

pack.description:
Pack is the connector pack's entry, nil when the pack does not
describe the column.

shape.description:
Shape is the column's effective shape (overlay, else pack, else
value) and TitleFrom and Mime its document rule when it is prose
or file.

shapes.description:
Shapes lists the shapes the column accepts, value first; a column
that can only be a value lists just value.

type.description: Type is the engine's own type string.

access_note.description:
AccessNote says that access is granted in Sercha, not inherited from
the source system.

connector.description: Connector is the connector id, for example "salesforce".

label.description: Label is the source system's name, for example "Salesforce".

mime.description:
Mime is the media type of a file column's documents (empty means
detect); prose documents are always text/plain.

shape.description:
Shape is the column's field shape: value, list, prose or file.
Empty on an overlay layer means the overlay leaves the shape alone.

title_from.description:
TitleFrom names the column that titles each document a prose or
file column derives.

unit.description: Unit is set only on a pack column layer.

catalogue.description: Catalogue is the table catalogue's own description, empty when none.

label.description: Label and Description are what readers see for the table.

overlay.description: Overlay is the tenant's table entry, nil when it has none.

pack.description:
Pack is the connector pack's table entry, nil for a table the pack
does not declare.

table.description: Table is the bare table name; Dataset is the FROM form, `data.<table>`.

updated_by.description:
UpdatedBy and UpdatedAt describe the most recent overlay write for
the table; empty and nil when it has no overlay.

bytes_scanned.description:
BytesScanned is the data an external dataset engine read for this
operator (dataset_scan only; the engine's billing unit). Zero elsewhere.

elapsed_ns.description: ElapsedNs is the wall-clock time spent in this operator in nanoseconds.

engine_query_id.description:
EngineQueryID is the external engine's id for the query this operator
ran (dataset_scan only), for tracing it in the engine's console.

operator_kind.description: OperatorKind is the operator type string, e.g. "CorpusScan", "EntityScan".

rows_in.description: RowsIn is the number of rows fed into this operator.

rows_out.description:
RowsOut is the number of rows emitted by this operator after filtering
and projection.

op_stats.description:
OpStats holds per-operator timing and row-count data, in execution order.
Each entry corresponds to one operator node in the plan tree.

row_count.description: RowCount is the number of rows in the result set.

PushDocumentRequest.description: One document to push into a push source

content.description:
Content is the document's raw bytes, base64-encoded. See
handlePushDocuments' doc comment for why base64-in-JSON was chosen
over multipart/form-data.

external_id.description:
ExternalID identifies this document within the source and is
caller-controlled. Re-pushing the same ExternalID updates the
existing document rather than creating a duplicate.

group.description:
Group is the document's partition key on a group-partitioned corpus:
the client, entity or fund it belongs to.

REQUIRED when a claiming corpus declares PARTITION BY GROUP. A push
source has one root container and no hierarchy, so a pushed document
derives no folder segments and would otherwise key to the empty string,
which means "visible to every partition". There is no safe default, so
an ungrouped document is rejected rather than filed arbitrarily.

Rejected when no claiming corpus is group-partitioned, so a caller
sending a group to a folder-partitioned corpus learns it is not
partitioning the way they think rather than having it silently ignored.
Enforced in resolveGroupKeys, not here: only the service knows which
corpora end up claiming the document.

Stored with the document even when no corpus claims it yet, so a
group-partitioned corpus created later claims it under this group
rather than finding it ungrouped. Validated at accept for that reason.

metadata.description: Metadata is optional connector-agnostic key/value metadata.

mime_type.description:
MimeType drives normaliser dispatch (PDF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, HTML,
Markdown, plain text, ...). Required: without it the normaliser
registry has nothing to key off.

path.description: Path is an optional display path or URL for the document.

title.description: Title is the document's display title.

PushDocumentResult.description: Per-document outcome of a push request

status.description:
Status is the document's ingest status at the moment the push
returned, which for an accepted document is always "processing" -
the bytes are retained and a sync of the source is queued to read
them, but nothing has been normalised, indexed or extracted yet.

This field is the honest half of the contract change described on
handlePushDocuments: a document_id no longer means "searchable now",
it means "accepted, ask later". Poll GET /api/v1/documents/{id} and
read ingest_status to find out when that changed.

Empty on a result that failed before acceptance, where there is no
document to have a status.

PushDocumentsRequest.description: Request body for pushing one or more documents to a push source

documents.description: Documents is one or more documents to ingest in this call.

mode.description:
Mode is the caller's explicit choice between per-document immediate
extraction ("single") and one accumulated extraction run spanning the
whole request ("batch"). Required, and deliberately not inferred from
len(documents): a caller pushing exactly one document from a poll
cycle that will send more shortly may still want "batch" semantics,
and a caller forwarding many latency-sensitive events one at a time
may still want "single" semantics for each. See driving.IngestMode's
doc comment for the full reasoning.

PushDocumentsResponse.description: Response body listing the per-document outcome of a push request

SourceDocumentsResponse.description: Paginated list of documents belonging to a source

confirm.description:
Confirm when true signals that the caller acknowledges the soft-call-limit
estimate returned in a prior 202 response and wishes to proceed with live
plugin calls. Default false; the query returns 202 if the limit is exceeded.

ir.description: IR is a JSON IR operator tree (same format as POST /api/v1/query/json-ir).

serchaql.description: SerchaQL is a SerchaQL text statement (or script).

notices.description:
Notices are the engine's messages about the result as a whole (such
as a NOT IN over a NULL, or withheld columns).

StartExportRequest.description: Start a large export of one read-only SELECT

max_rows.description: MaxRows lowers the server's row cap for this export.

sql.description: SQL is one read-only SerchaQL SELECT.

wait_seconds.description:
WaitSeconds waits up to this long (max 60) for the export to finish
before answering.

notices.description:
Notices are the engine's messages about the result as a whole (such
as a NOT IN over a NULL, or withheld columns).
